packages.label_en: Teiku and Lacking Repair — The State of Exile
packages.reason: Teiku (the unresolved Talmudic question marker) and mechusar tikkun (lacking repair/completion) share the same essential nature: both are expressions of the unrectified, incomplete, exilic state. They are not cause-and-effect — one does not produce the other. Rather, they are two faces of the same phenomenon: the absence of the nun of tikkun. Teiku IS mechusar tikkun (the Zohar declares this identity directly). The entire Torah is built on this single bechina. The kinot (lamentations) belong to the same domain — same letters as tikkun but with the nun bent, the visual embodiment of the fallen/exile state. The polarity is evil/deficient: this cluster represents what is broken, unrectified, and in exile, in contrast to the aspired-to state of tikkun (repair) which is the implicit good pole of the teaching.

good_evil_mirror.mirror_note: The positive pole of this Torah is תִּיקּוּן (complete repair) — the state where the nun is upright and present. This is the aspired-to state, stated explicitly at the end of the Torah ('may the kinot be transformed into tikkun'). However, tikkun itself does not appear as a dataset node for Torah #247 — it is the goal, not yet catalogued. A future package around תִּיקּוּן and the upright נ would be its mirror.
